html:
The Gunditjmara are an Aboriginal people of southwestern Victoria, around today's Warrnambool, Port Fairy and Portland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their Country holds Budj Bim, a volcano whose lava flow they shaped into a system of channels, weirs and ponds for trapping and keeping short-finned eels. Parts of it are at least 6,600 years old, which makes it one of the oldest aquaculture systems in the world. Stone house foundations stand nearby, so this was a settled life, not a wandering one. Budj Bim became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019.

Whalers and sealers reached the coast in the early 1800s. At the Convincing Ground near Portland, whalers killed many Gunditjmara in a fight over a stranded whale in the 1830s. When settlers took the land, the Gunditjmara fought back for years in the Eumeralla Wars. Neighbours included the Jardwadjali and the Djargurd Wurrung. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Gunditjmara are an Aboriginal people of southwestern Victoria, around today's Warrnambool, Port Fairy and Portland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.
